title: Trump criticises Schumer amid push for new Democrat leadership in US Senate
text:
Trump criticises Schumer amid push for new Democrat leadership in US Senate
Schumer, who has led the Democratic caucus since 2017, faces a challenge from Chris Van Hollen in his bid to be the next Senate majority leader.
Chuck Schumer, the top Democrat in the United States Senate, is facing backlash against his bid to serve as Senate majority leader in the incoming Congress.
On Sunday, President Donald Trump added to the ongoing criticism of Schumer’s leadership, signalling there would be tension with the White House if Schumer were picked again to lead the Democratic caucus.
“It is going to be very hard for me to work with Chuck Schumer should he become Senate Majority Leader,” Trump wrote on Truth Social.
“He failed badly as ‘Leader’ once before, one of the worst in history, and I have little doubt that he will fail again.”
The debate over Schumer’s leadership has underscored divides within the Democratic Party, particularly in the wake of the November 3 midterm elections.
Following a historic set of victories, Democrats are set to take control of both chambers of Congress in January.
Schumer, who leads the Democratic Senate minority, is hoping to retain his leadership position. A closed-door, secret-ballot vote is scheduled for December 1 to decide the majority leader.
A senator representing New York since 1999, Schumer has expressed confidence in his odds, saying he has the necessary votes to stay in charge.
“I will be elected majority leader,” Schumer told reporters last week.
But critics say Schumer, who will turn 76 on Monday, is ill-suited to lead a Senate Democratic caucus increasingly shaped by younger, anti-establishment lawmakers.
Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen, backed by progressives, has mounted a campaign to challenge Schumer for the majority leader role.
Van Hollen told NBC’s Meet the Press on Sunday that he, too, was confident of winning.
“If you look at our caucus, you can see a huge appetite for change. They are seeing the American people and the Democratic Party calling for change. They also want to change the way we do business in the United States Democratic caucus and the United States Senate,” he said.
Schumer has also seen falling public approval ratings. In mid-November, a poll by the news agency Reuters and the research firm Ipsos found that 34 percent of self-identified Democrats viewed Schumer favourably. That percentage was down from 38 percent in February.
November’s poll also suggested that 43 percent of Democrats held an unfavourable view of Schumer, who has led Senate Democrats since 2017.
The Senate Democratic leader is the only unresolved role among Congress’s top four positions.
House Democrats last week nominated Hakeem Jeffries to be speaker in the next Congress.
Meanwhile, John Thune will continue to lead Senate Republicans, and Representative Jim Jordan will succeed Speaker Mike Johnson as the top House Republican.

title: Trump to host private dinner for largest owners of his meme coin
text:
Trump to host private dinner for largest owners of his meme coin
Sunday’s dinner is the third private event for top holders of the $Trump meme coin, launched shortly before his second inauguration.
United States President Donald Trump will host a third private dinner for top investors in his meme coin $TRUMP, reigniting questions about potential conflicts of interest with his cryptocurrency ventures.
Sunday’s gala will take place at the Trump National Golf Club outside Washington, DC.
According to the dinner’s official website, the top 185 meme-coin holders will be invited to a gala dinner, where guests will include businessman Kevin O’Leary and boxer Floyd Mayweather.
The top 29 holders, meanwhile, will be given special access to a VIP reception where Trump will reportedly be present.
“There will be no private meetings with The President. No gifts will be accepted,” the website said of the VIP reception.
The event has been billed as “a once-in-a-lifetime experience — an evening you will talk about forever”.
But Democrats have accused the Republican leader of leveraging his public office for profit in violation of federal law. They see such dinners as an opportunity for private interests to pay for access to the president.
“Trump is continuing to exploit the presidency for his personal gain,” Kendall Witmer, the deputy communications director for the Democratic National Committee, said in a statement.
In October, shortly after the gala was announced, eight Democratic senators issued an open letter promising to investigate any conflicts of interest such an event might raise.
“President Trump’s continued monetization of his name and likeness once again raises serious ethical concerns, necessitating this request for a robust inquiry into the President’s financial entanglements and personal profiteering,” the letter said.
The Democratic Party has since won majorities in both chambers of Congress in the November 3 midterm race, paving the way for possible inquiries and subpoenas when the new members are sworn in next year.
Trump’s White House has dismissed the criticism, calling the dinner a “private event, not a government function”. It has also emphasised that “there is no promise of official government action in exchange for attending”.
Trump has also argued that many of his assets are held in a trust while he is in office, though that trust is largely run by his family members.
The president is a stakeholder in cryptocurrency firms like World Liberty Financial, and has made promoting cryptocurrency a central part of his second term.
Under his leadership, the US Treasury established a reserve of digital currency assets, as part of Trump’s effort to make the US the “crypto capital of the world”.
Sunday’s gala is believed to be the third such dinner for top $Trump meme coin holders.
Meme coins trade on a popular likeness from the internet. Trump launched his on January 17, 2025, days before the start of his second term.
To encourage meme-coin purchases, Trump and his business partners held private events on May 22, 2025, and again on April 25, 2026, for top holders of the cryptocurrency.
The first was held at the same Trump golf club outside Washington, DC, and the second took place at Mar-a-Lago, Trump’s Florida resort.
The May 2025 dinner reportedly required a minimum of $55,000 in $Trump coins to attend.
At the time, Chinese crypto investor Justin Sun was declared the winner of a “contest” for who held the most $TRUMP coins. Sun held about $18m of the coin in 2025, as well as tokens from World Liberty Financial.
Earlier this year, Sun sued World Liberty Financial, saying it had frozen his access to the assets he owned with it, making it impossible for him to sell them.
Trump’s inauguration in January 2025 proved a major boost for his coin, pushing its value to $74.
The $Trump coin has since lost value. On the eve of the gala dinner, it is worth about $0.88.
According to financial disclosure forms released earlier this year, Trump earned more than $2.2bn in 2025, the first year of his second term.
Much of that wealth came from meme coins, tokens and other digital assets. Some $636m came from $Trump meme coin sales.

title: Democrats win largest House majority since 1992 with North Carolina seat
text:
Democrats win largest House majority since 1992 with North Carolina seat
At least 258 US House seats are now under Democratic control, with four more midterm races yet to be decided.
The Democratic Party has won at least 258 seats in the United States House of Representatives, its highest total since 1992.
On Sunday, a congressional race in North Carolina was decided after a recount, giving Democrats their 258th House seat, as a handful of races in the 2026 midterm elections are still being counted.
The race for North Carolina’s 5th congressional district saw Democrat Chuck Hubbard defeat Republican incumbent Virginia Foxx, who has served 11 terms in Congress.
The win was symbolic of a larger political shift in North Carolina and elsewhere, as longtime Republican strongholds flipped to Democratic hands, sometimes for the first time in decades.
Foxx was first elected in 2004, and in recent years, she was the chair of the House Rules Committee. According to The Associated Press news agency, only 330 votes separated Hubbard and Foxx as of Sunday, when the race was called in the Democrat’s favour.
Four House races have yet to be called, meaning Democrats may still expand their already sizeable majority in the 435-member House.
The party has now picked up about 47 House seats. Currently, in the outgoing Congress, Democrats hold 214 seats.
But the House was not the only congressional chamber to flip in this year’s midterm elections.
In the 120th Congress, set to be sworn in on January 3, Democrats will also hold 56 seats in the US Senate, its largest majority in more than a decade.
Those majorities give the Democratic Party significant power over legislation, although President Donald Trump, a Republican, has already pledged to veto bills the party puts forward.
Experts say the Republican Party’s drubbing in the midterm elections was driven by voter frustration with issues like the cost of living, the US-Israel war on Iran, corruption and immigration raids.
It was also widely interpreted as a referendum on Trump’s second term, which began in 2025.
As of November, only 32 percent of Americans approved of Trump’s job performance, according to a poll by the news agency Reuters and the research firm Ipsos.
Democrats have framed their electoral victory as a unique opportunity to shape the final two years of Trump’s presidency.
Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, a progressive who won her re-election bid in New York’s 14th congressional district, called the political shift a “mandate for change”.
“This is a historic moment for our country. This is one of the largest classes we have seen,” Ocasio-Cortez said at the US Capitol.
The party’s majority in the House will be larger than any since Democrat Bill Clinton was first elected president in 1992 with a 258-seat majority for his party.
It is also just above the 257 seats held by Democrats when Barack Obama was elected in 2008.

title: Netanyahu’s Likud, Eisenkot’s Yashar end coalition talks without deal
text:
Netanyahu’s Likud, Eisenkot’s Yashar end coalition talks without deal
Parties remain split on who will lead the next government and whether far right minister Itamar Ben-Gvir will join.
Talks between the parties of caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form a unity government have ended without a deal.
Representatives of Netanyahu’s Likud and Eisenkot’s Yashar parties met in a Herzliya hotel on Sunday, where they remained split on who would lead the next government and whether far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir would be part of it, according to Israel’s Channel 12 broadcaster.
The Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper reported that Likud wanted Ben-Gvir in government, while Yashar insisted on his exclusion.
In a joint statement, the two parties said they had “outlined their positions on a range of substantive issues” and that a “follow-up meeting would be held”, without revealing a date or any further details.
Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government, with the possibility of a 14-day extension, after the elections in October gave his bloc 48 seats – 13 short of a majority.
Netanyahu has called for a unity government, saying it was the only way that Israel’s security could be guaranteed. Such an arrangement would allow a government to be formed without the inclusion of parties led by Palestinian citizens of Israel, which won a record 19 seats.
Channel 12 reported that former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, who leads the Together list, proposed a coalition of Together, Yashar, Likud and Avigdor Lieberman’s Yisrael Beiteinu, with Eisenkot serving first and Netanyahu succeeding him.
However, Eisenkot has opposed a rotation, and Netanyahu has reportedly insisted on taking the premiership first, while Lieberman has ruled out joining any government that includes Netanyahu altogether.
If unity talks fail, Yashar plans to seek a confidence vote in the Knesset for a minority government before Eisenkot’s mandate expires. It would rely on outside support from the Arab Joint List, led by Yousef Jabareen, and the United Arab List, led by Mansour Abbas.

title: Heartbreak in US capital as Washington Spirit lose women’s football final
text:
Heartbreak in US capital as Washington Spirit lose women’s football final
KC Current win NWSL championship as Spirit lose third consecutive final despite playing in front of rowdy home crowd.
Washington, DC – Trinity Rodman sat on the pitch and held her face in her hands, trying to hold back tears as the final whistle ended her Washington Spirit’s quest for the National Women’s Soccer League (NWSL) with a 2-1 loss to the Kansas City Current.
For Rodman, who could be seen wincing in pain throughout the match after an early shoulder injury, the loss in the final on Saturday night was a familiar feeling. She and the Spirit had reached, but lost, the two previous finals.
This one, however, was different. The Spirit were playing in front of their home fans – a sold-out crowd at Audi Field in Washington, DC, and palpable support across the city.
The third time was not the charm for the Spirit.
The stakes were high on Saturday night with a huge turnout at the stadium and increased interest in women’s football across the country. Former footballer Tobin Heath compared the NWSL to the National Football League (NFL), the most-watched sports league in the US.
And with their cult-like following, the Spirit were hoping to leave local fans with a memory of sporting glory that would last a lifetime.
“The ladies fought hard. I don’t think it was the best performance, but they fought hard. They fought to the end. They were still in it in the 90-something minute, but I wish they would have won,” Spirit fan Angel Ughiovhe told Al Jazeera.
After the KC Current went 2-0 up, Rodman had clawed a goal back in the dying moments of the match, cutting the deficit in half, giving fans a glimmer of hope for a historic comeback that never materialised.
“We were saying internally, third time is a charm,” Kim Bolt, chief marketing and strategy officer at the Washington Spirit, told Al Jazeera on Friday.
“I think especially because our fans mean so much to us, it would just be absolutely incredible if we could get the win in front of our, you know, rowdy Audi crowd.”
That belief was shared across the city. But it just wasn’t meant to be.
Despite the defeat, the final highlighted the passion for women’s football in the US capital and the adoration for the local team.
The soaring arches of the Frederick Douglass Memorial Bridge glowed with the team’s green and pink colours ahead of the final. People across the city walked around with the team’s top that features Washington’s famous cherry blossom. Even the public buses said, “Go Spirit!”
For many Spirit fans, the final was more than a game. Chants of “Free DC” rang out in the stadium at the end of the 51st minute as they have for the past year since President Donald Trump deployed federal troops in the city.
The chant, which is timed to reflect DC’s quest to become the 51st US state, was echoed by spectators outside the stadium at nearby watch parties, highlighting the popularity of the political culture that fans had built around the team.
The capital city is home to nearly 700,000 people who do not have voting members in Congress because DC is not a state.
Carlene Reid said she was disappointed by the outcome of the match on Saturday but she took solace in that people across the country heard the demand for DC statehood.
“This is probably the most inclusive game I’ve ever come to and the most politically sound game,” Reid told Al Jazeera.
“It was absolutely amazing to hear the chant happen as a DC resident. So I’m happy that the message is getting out there that we are fighting for statehood.”
KC Current midfielder Vanessa DiBernardo scored directly from a corner in the 54th minute on Saturday shortly after the stadium erupted with the politically charged chant. Brazilian legend Debinha added a second for the champions from a counterattack in the 97th minute.
Rodman scored from a header minutes later.
The win cements Kansas City’s status as a football hub for the men’s and women’s games. Despite its relatively small population of 520,000 people, the city also has a team in the country’s top men’s football league, Major League Soccer (MLS), and it hosted six FIFA World Cup matches over the summer.
Football has been growing in popularity in the US, especially after Argentinian legend Lionel Messi joined Inter Miami in 2023. Cohosting the World Cup with Canada and Mexico only accelerated that trend. The US also hosted the Club World Cup in 2025.
Bolt said the surging interest in men’s football has not come at the expense of the women’s game.
“We have our own fan base that is passionate, that is hungry for content, that is hungry for our merch, hungry for our ticket sales,” Bolt told Al Jazeera.
“The growth in the men’s game – we’re not seeing that cannibalise or stunt our own growth because I think the fan bases are pretty unique.”
Attendance at Spirit’s home games at Audi Field – a 20,000-seat stadium – backs that theory. The Spirit played in front of sold-out crowds in the quarterfinal and semifinal.
And there wasn’t an empty seat on Saturday night despite the skyrocketing ticket prices, which started at more than $300 on the resale market.
The Spirit partnered with DC Mayor-elect Janeese Lewis George to give away 400 tickets through a raffle.
Audi Field on Saturday featured some of the top players in the game between the two squads, who could play key roles for their national teams at the Women’s World Cup in Brazil next year.
On the Current side, Croix Bethune and Michelle Cooper are likely to feature for the US Women’s National Team (USWNT). Temwa Chawinga, who led Malawi to the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) final earlier this year, is expected to lead her country at the World Cup.
For the Spirit, Rodman was a young, rising star at the last tournament, but she heads into next year as one of the most renowned players in the sport as the USWNT push to reclaim the title from Spain.
The Spirit’s number 10, Leicy Santos, is also set to shine on the international stage with Colombia, while defender Esme Morgan is likely to be called up for England. Sandy MacIver is expected to start between the sticks for Scotland.
Algeria’s Melissa Bethi could also feature at the tournament after her team secured qualification by reaching the WAFCON semifinals.
“One of the best things about DC is that it is an international city,” Bolt said.
“We love the fact that our team is a reflection of the city, the diversity of the city – that we have so many international players.”

title: Liverpool 4-0 Manchester United: Five key takeaways for Pochettino
text:
Liverpool 4-0 Manchester United: Five key takeaways for Pochettino
United suffer their worst result under a new manager in 100 years as Liverpool cruise past Mauricio Pochettino’s side.
If Mauricio Pochettino had any doubt about the size of the job in front of him at Manchester United, his players confirmed his worst fears within 13 minutes of his first game in charge – a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool.
As the home side surged into a two-goal lead in the opening exchanges at Anfield, with the away side reduced to 10 men, the sinking sensation for United – who are second bottom of the Premier League – immediately returned.
Any ‘new-manager bounce’, as feared by Reds manager Andoni Iraola, had no time to materialise with a rash challenge from Lenny Yoro on Alexander Isak leading to a straight red in the eighth minute.
The resulting free-kick was powered home by Dominik Szoboszlai, with Florian Wirtz thereafter converting a sharp attack in a flash – ending the match as a contest.
Pochettino slammed the decision to send off Yoro after the game, but there was a familiar feeling about the performance overall.
Al Jazeera Sport takes a look at five key takeaways as the opening salvo of the ninth manager since United’s last league title in 2013 fell apart – resulting in the worst start for a new manager of the club in 100 years.
Was the referee right to send off Manchester United’s Lenny Yoro?
Even though United have greater concerns, the answer was undoubtedly: no. The question for the referee, in sending off Yoro for denying a goalscoring opportunity, had four considerations: distance between the offence and the goal, general direction of the play, likelihood of keeping or gaining control of the ball, and location and number of defenders.
Of those guidelines, the most pertinent were the direction of play, which was at an angle across the box, and the likelihood of keeping control of the ball – Isak arguably had no control of it at all after a heavy first touch that allowed United keeper Senne Lammens to gather.
VAR (video assistant referee) had the chance to ask the referee to reconsider his decision, but decided there was no clear and obvious error. Had the referee reviewed the red card, then he would have surely decided a yellow card would have sufficed.
The play that led to the card being shown, however, was even more questionable than the outcome.
Was Pochettino right to bench Maguire for Man United?
The release of the team sheets, an hour and 15 minutes before kickoff, was the first moment all United fans looked to.
For all the pre-game comments by Pochettino, the Argentinean’s starting 11 was always going to be the first true sense of his evaluation of United’s current woes.
Dropping defender Harry Maguire, a former club captain, was a massive call – all the more so given the inexperience of Yoro and Matthijs de Ligt, who were both selected ahead of the ex-England stalwart.
The ref’s mistake in sending off Yoro was clear, but Yoro and de Ligt were heavily exposed in the play that led to the sending-off.
The latter is easing his way back into first-team action after a year out with a back injury and found himself in no-man’s land as Isak chased a long ball. Yoro sought to cover, but was clumsy and ill-advised in his attempt, allowing Isak to draw what was only a soft challenge and connection.
United were plucky after the change forced by the sending-off, with Maguire replacing the clearly, and understandably, disappointed Bryan Mbeumo.
Maguire’s fine, last-ditch block from Isak’s close-range pivot and shot saved United’s blushes five minutes before the break, and made Pochettino’s first big call look all the worse.
A scuffed attempt at a clearance early in the second half by de Ligt allowed Isak clean through only for the Liverpool forward to slice his effort.
By the time Rio Ngumoha added a 66th-minute third, all the questions about a defence that had previously shipped 30 goals in 15 games this season had been answered. The fourth from Victor Munoz was inevitable, and it could have been a lot worse for United on the day.
Their last defeat at Anfield was a 7-0 victory for the home side – a repeat was certainly possible had Liverpool been more clinical.
Matters were so bad that the former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher commented on Sky Sports that he “felt sorry” for de Ligt prior to his eventual substitution in the second half.
The consensus was that Pochettino made the wrong call before the start.
What other Man United changes did Pochettino make at Liverpool?
Yoro and de Ligt have been peripheral figures in their time with the Old Trafford club, for varying reasons including injury, but they were not the only big calls made by Pochettino.
Another injury-plagued player, Patrick Dorgu, was also given a start – and in a formation which was not wholly clear. The popular Amad Diallo was forced to make do with a place on the bench alongside Maguire.
Dorgu, whose form has been indifferent at best, can operate as a wide defender or attacker. It appeared as though he was given some licence on the left to get forward, with United reverting to a back four, Lisandro Martinez covering on the flank in defence and Diogo Dalot holding back on the right.
Whether it was a back four or five to begin with – the latter explaining the absence of the more forward-minded Diallo – United were quickly forced to a five with the sending-off and the sacrifice of Mbeumo at the other end of the pitch.
Not only was the decision to pick two less experienced centre-backs at Anfield a monumental – and ultimately costly – call, the move to switch to an unfamiliar feel across the backline was a painful lesson for Pochettino, who himself is more accustomed to a 4-2-3-1 setup.
What next for Manchester United and Mauricio Pochettino?
With 19th-placed United mired in the Premier League drop zone, the UEFA Champions League appears a sideshow, but a trip to Sporting Lisbon awaits on Wednesday.
In some ways, Europe’s elite club competition, which United have returned to after a three-year absence, may well give Pochettino a free hit to explore how he can get the best out of a beleaguered group.
The absolute priority for the Red Devils has to be channelling their efforts towards climbing the domestic ladder and pulling well away from an unthinkable relegation scrap.
Yoro will be available for the match in the Portuguese capital, which means Pochettino must wrestle with his decision to pick the young duo in defence. Failing to pick both Yoro and de Ligt at Sporting would almost appear an early admission of error.
What is the wider context for Manchester United and Pochettino?
Former United captain Roy Keane was at Anfield as a pundit for Sky Sports and, in his analysis of the overall display, described his old club’s performance at Anfield as “desperate”.
Harsh words for the current playing group are nothing new. Their latest low leaves them with the worst defensive record in top-flight football in Europe.
Pochettino at least has time on his side to reverse United’s worst league start in 40 years, but some short-term solutions will be expected by the time Brentford arrive at Old Trafford next Saturday.
Should Pochettino not find some considerable longer-term strategies soon, then the desperate may well turn to the unimaginable.
The heat is turning up for the Red Devils, and the patience of the fans has already run thin with the players this season.
The much-maligned ownership of the Glazer family and Jim Ratcliffe’s Ineos group can also expect prolonged protests, as seen of late.
Change in the dugout appears as though it will not be anywhere near enough to reverse a trend 13 years in the making – and the fans’ unswerving support of Pochettino’s predecessor, Michael Carrick, attests to the fact that wholesale reformation is warranted.

title: MacKenzie Scott gives $62 million to protect tropical oceans and support 10,000 communities
text:
MacKenzie Scott has donated $62 million to Blue Ventures, a marine conservation organisation working with small-scale fishing communities and local groups across tropical regions. Announced on December 10, 2025, the funding will support efforts to protect marine ecosystems, improve fisheries management and strengthen the livelihoods of people who depend on the ocean. It will contribute to the organisation's 2030 strategy, which aims to enable 10,000 fishing communities to lead marine conservation and fisheries management. The plan also seeks to bring 200,000 square kilometres of carbon-rich seas under effective local stewardship and improve food security and economic resilience for five million people. A significant proportion of the donation will support local organisations through the Frontline Community Fund.
How MacKenzie Scott’s  $62 million donation will be used
The funding will support Blue Ventures' long-term work with coastal communities, allowing local organisations to expand conservation initiatives and respond to environmental and economic challenges. These include warming seas, declining fish catches and growing uncertainty over fishing-related livelihoods.
A significant proportion of the donation will be channelled to local partners through the Frontline Community Fund, which provides flexible, long-term financial support to organisations working directly with fishing communities. The funding model is intended to give these groups greater control over their priorities rather than restricting them to narrowly defined, short-term projects.
Blue Ventures will work with local partners and Regional Advisory Councils to determine funding priorities. Its approach places particular emphasis on transparency, accountability and community leadership, with local knowledge playing an important role in decisions about marine resource management.
What is Blue Ventures and where does it work?
Founded in 2003, Blue Ventures has spent more than two decades working alongside small-scale fishing communities and local organisations across the tropics. Its work focuses on helping communities manage fisheries sustainably, restore marine ecosystems and protect livelihoods dependent on coastal resources.
The organisation began its work in Madagascar and has since developed programmes and partnerships across several tropical regions, including East Africa, West Africa, Southeast Asia and the Western Indian Ocean.
Its conservation activities include supporting locally managed marine areas, restoring mangrove forests and seagrass habitats, improving fisheries monitoring and helping communities participate in decisions concerning their coastal waters.
Rather than treating conservation as an activity separate from local livelihoods, Blue Ventures works with fishing communities to develop management approaches that protect marine resources while supporting the people who depend on them.
Why small-scale fishing communities are central to marine conservation
More than 100 million people worldwide rely on small-scale fishing for their daily food and livelihoods, according to Blue Ventures. These communities depend heavily on healthy coastal ecosystems, including coral reefs, mangroves and seagrass meadows.
Coral reefs provide habitats for fish and other marine species, while mangroves serve as important nursery grounds for marine life and help protect coastlines from storms and erosion. Seagrass meadows also support marine biodiversity and store carbon.
However, these ecosystems face growing pressure from overfishing, habitat degradation and climate change. Rising ocean temperatures and declining fish populations can affect catches, reduce household incomes and threaten local food supplies.
Blue Ventures' approach involves supporting communities in monitoring and managing their fisheries, restoring damaged habitats and developing locally led conservation measures. The organisation believes that giving fishing communities a greater role in managing marine resources can help protect ecosystems while maintaining the livelihoods they support.
What is the Frontline Community Fund?
The Frontline Community Fund is a Blue Ventures initiative designed to direct financial support towards grassroots organisations working with coastal communities. It aims to address the difficulty smaller organisations often face in accessing long-term conservation funding.
Through the fund, local organisations can receive flexible financial assistance, technical support and opportunities to share knowledge with other community groups. The initiative also supports the development of community-led data systems that help fishers monitor catches, understand changes in local ecosystems and make informed decisions about fisheries management.
Regional Advisory Councils are another part of the model. These councils bring together representatives with local knowledge and experience to help guide funding priorities and identify organisations that could benefit from support.
In 2025, Blue Ventures launched its first Regional Advisory Council for the Asia-Pacific region in Bali, Indonesia. The council brought together seven representatives from local organisations in Indonesia and the Philippines. The organisation intends to develop similar structures in other regions.
Blue Ventures' 2030 conservation targets
The $62 million donation will contribute to a broader strategy aimed at expanding community-led marine conservation across tropical coastal regions by 2030.
The organisation's targets include enabling 10,000 fishing communities to lead fisheries management and marine conservation, bringing 200,000 square kilometres of carbon-rich seas under effective local stewardship and improving food security and economic resilience for five million people.
It also aims to equip hundreds of communities and grassroots organisations with the funding, skills, data and advocacy support needed to sustain their conservation work.
The strategy focuses on building partnerships with local organisations so that conservation initiatives can expand while remaining rooted in the needs and knowledge of individual communities.
The donation strengthens Blue Ventures' ability to support these efforts, with the organisation seeking to expand existing partnerships and help coastal communities take a leading role in protecting marine ecosystems and securing their livelihoods.

title: US targets Beverly Hills mansion linked to Iraq and Syria fuel contracts
text:
US authorities are seeking to seize a Beverly Hills mansion allegedly bought and renovated with money linked to a scheme involving more than $700 million in US military fuel contracts. The US Department of Justice filed a civil forfeiture complaint in the Central District of California. The complaint alleges that a Virginia-based defence contractor and others obtained the money from the US Department of Defense’s Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) between 2016 and 2020. According to the US Department of Justice, about $30 million from the scheme was transferred in 2018 to buy the property, with further spending on renovations and improvements between 2019 and 2022. It also alleges that the scheme involved bribes to an Iraqi official for exclusive access to deliver jet fuel.
How the alleged $700 million military fuel scheme operated
According to the complaint, a Virginia-based defence contractor and others took part in the scheme between 2016 and 2020. They allegedly obtained more than $700 million from the Defense Logistics Agency for fuel deliveries to US forces during ‘Operation Inherent Resolve’, the US campaign against the Islamic State of Iraq and Syria.
The deliveries were made in Iraq and Syria, with Erbil International Airport (EIA) in Kurdistan serving as a critical fuel delivery point for US forces. Kurdish Peshmerga forces provided internal security and controlled access to the facility.
The complaint alleges that the contractor’s officers agreed to pay General Mansour Barzani, a senior Peshmerga official, $0.25 per litre in exchange for exclusive access to deliver jet fuel in Kurdistan for US military and coalition forces. The contractor then received hundreds of millions of dollars under DLA contracts.
Around $30 million was transferred to buy and renovate the Beverly Hills mansion
The complaint alleges that the contractor’s competitors were prevented from accessing Erbil International Airport to deliver jet fuel for the Defense Logistics Agency. The agency issued one-time-buy contracts to the contractor, often at noncompetitive and inflated prices. Funds received from the agency were allegedly transferred to NYJD Trust No.1, a trust established in Virginia for the private benefit of Barzani.
In 2018, approximately $30 million from those funds was transferred to purchase the property. That money was also used for renovation and improvement work on the property between 2019 and 2022.
FBI and other US agencies investigated the Beverly Hills mansion case
The case was investigated by the FBI Washington Field Office, the Defense Criminal Investigative Service, and IRS Criminal Investigation. Deputy Chief Michael B. Redmann and Senior Trial Attorney Steven Parker of the Justice Department’s Money Laundering, Narcotics and Forfeiture Section are handling the case.
The US Attorney’s Office for the Central District of California and the Justice Department’s Office of International Affairs also provided support. Reportedly, the civil complaint contains allegations and does not itself establish that the property is subject to forfeiture. The government must prove, by a preponderance of the evidence, that the mansion is subject to forfeiture.
Disclaimer: This article is based on the civil forfeiture complaint filed by the US Department of Justice in the Beverly Hills mansion case. The Times of India has not independently verified the allegations of the military fuel contract scheme or the claims made against the individuals involved.

title: Scientists find timber rattlesnakes wait weeks near winter shelters
text:
Timber rattlesnakes spend much of the year near underground shelters where they escape the cold winter months. A study found that the snakes also spend several weeks waiting near these shelters before entering them in autumn and moving away in spring. Researchers monitored 38 timber rattlesnakes, 20 of them fitted with radio transmitters, in Jersey County, Illinois, over two autumns and two springs to understand this behaviour. They found that temperature may have influenced when the snakes arrived, entered their shelters, and left in warmer weather.
According to the research published in Ecology and Evolution titled ‘
Fall and Spring Staging in a Refugia‐Dependent Migratory Snake
’, the snakes spent more than 6 months inside their winter shelters. Including the waiting periods before and after winter, their association with these shelters lasted nearly 8 months.
Timber rattlesnakes spend weeks near winter shelters before entering
The researchers found that the snakes did not move directly from their summer ranges into underground refuges. In autumn, they first reached the overwintering habitat and stayed nearby before entering. This fall staging period averaged 29.23 days in 2021, but was shorter in 2022, at 8.2 days. Of 27 paired seasonal records from 17 snakes, 6 animals entered refuges on the day they arrived.
The other 21 remained on the surface before going underground. They sheltered beneath leaves, rocks, or hollow logs, at an average distance of 58.17 metres from refuges. They used an average of 1.91 locations and stayed at each for about 12.29 days. Entry took place mainly at night at the monitored refuges in Jersey County.
PC: Ecology and Evolution 
Why do timber rattlesnakes wait near winter shelters after emerging in spring
Spring brought a second pause after the snakes emerged from their underground refuges. Rather than immediately moving towards their summer habitats, the radio-tracked animals stayed in nearby bluff areas. The spring staging period averaged 21.81 days in 2022 and 26.35 days in 2023. Researchers recorded 31 paired seasonal records from 20 tracked snakes.
After emerging, the snakes concealed themselves beneath leaves, rocks and hollow logs, an average of 75.50 metres from their overwintering refuges. They occupied an average of 2.4 locations and remained at each for about 10.63 days. Some returned to staging locations they had used during the previous autumn or in earlier years. Most emerged at night, although a smaller midday peak was recorded during the monitoring period.
How do temperature changes influence rattlesnakes' seasonal movements
Temperature measurements showed different conditions for the snakes’ arrival, entry, emergence and departure. In autumn, they reached overwintering habitat at an average temperature near 19°C, but entered refuges at about 14°C. In spring, they emerged at around 14°C and began moving towards summer habitats at approximately 19°C.
The researchers found that snakes began entering refuges after a rapid fall in temperature. Spring departures followed a sharp and sustained rise over several consecutive days. Emergence was staggered, as snakes came out during warm periods before colder weather interrupted activity. The study suggests temperature may be an important cue for these movements, although the authors said further data would be needed to assess other influences across the two years covered in each season.
Staging periods help snakes navigate seasonal temperature changes
The authors describe the pauses as staging periods that separate migration from entry into or exit from winter refuges. They suggest these intervals may act as buffers, helping snakes match seasonal movements with suitable temperatures. In autumn, arriving early may allow the reptiles to reach shelter before conditions become too cold, while delaying entry leaves time for remaining active-season opportunities.
In spring, emerging before moving away may reduce the risk of travelling during cold conditions. The researchers said this behaviour could help temperate reptiles manage unpredictable seasonal changes. However, they noted that the study could not establish every reason for staging, and that additional multi-year research is needed to examine the role of temperature alongside other environmental or internal factors.

title: Woman wins £5,131 after Harrods refused refund for £4,550 Cartier bracelet
text:
A woman who bought a £4,550 Cartier bracelet from Harrods has won a court battle against the luxury retailer after it refused to refund her, claiming the returned item had scratches. Georgia Romain, a hypnotherapist from Kingston upon Thames, had returned the 18-carat gold bracelet because it was too small for her wrist. However, after Harrods rejected her return and questioned the bracelet's condition, she challenged the decision in court without legal representation. Deputy District Judge Elaine Vignoli ruled that the retailer had failed to prove the bracelet was returned damaged, ordering Harrods to pay her £5,131, including interest and court fees.
Harrods denied a refund for a £4,550 Cartier bracelet over alleged scratches
After receiving the bracelet, Harrods' customer service team rejected the return, claiming that the item had been damaged and had scratches on its surface. The retailer told Ms Romain that the bracelet would be transferred to its lost property department unless she reclaimed it within 30 days. The dispute centred on Harrods' claim that the alleged damage meant the 18-carat gold bangle could no longer be resold.
According to The Independent, the retailer's customer service team had recorded a "pre-inspection video" of the bracelet after it was returned and examined. 
The video was used to identify what Harrods described as scratches and defects on the item's soft metal. However, Ms Romain questioned whether the bracelet shown in the footage was actually the one she had purchased, pointing out that the video did not show its unique serial number.
Harrods told woman her rejected Cartier bracelet was legally her property
After watching the video in August 2025, Ms Romain emailed Harrods to challenge the evidence being used to reject her return. She asked: "How can I be sure this is the same item because it doesn't show its unique serial number?" She also raised concerns about the appearance of the bracelet in the footage, saying that "the bracelet you’re holding in the pre-inspection video appears thicker than the one I ordered".
However, the retailer's subsequent response did not address her concerns about the missing serial number or the video. Instead, Harrods informed her that the return had been "formally rejected" and that the bracelet "is legally now your property". Ms Romain subsequently brought a claim against the department store at Mayor's and City County Court, seeking a refund or replacement under the Consumer Contracts Regulations.
Judge ruled Harrods failed to prove the returned Cartier bracelet had scratches
The case was heard by Deputy District Judge Elaine Vignoli, who examined the evidence presented by both sides. Harrods' lawyers argued that the bracelet would have been "secured safely and handled carefully along the way". However, the judge questioned the lack of evidence supporting the retailer's account of how the item had been handled after it was returned.
In her ruling, Judge Vignoli said: "For Harrods’ defence to succeed, I must be satisfied on the balance of probabilities that when they received the bracelet from Ms Romain it contained the same damage and the same scratches." She added: "But I am afraid there was a lack of evidence from the defendants before me today to satisfy me on that point." The judge subsequently determined that Harrods had not established that the bracelet was returned with scratches.
Harrods failed to prove the scratched Cartier bracelet had lost its resale value
The judge also questioned the department store's position that the alleged scratches had made the bracelet worthless. Harrods had argued that it could not resell the item because of its condition, but the court heard that the retailer had failed to provide solid evidence demonstrating how the alleged defects affected its value.
According to The Independent, Judge Vignoli also challenged the retailer's argument over the bracelet's resale value, saying: "Harrods said that the bracelet is worth nothing to us because we can’t resell it, but I’m not quite sure I can agree with that – if it is genuinely worthless I would happily take it home with me." The judge described the bracelet as a "rather pretty, luxurious item" and concluded that the retailer's evidence had been insufficient.
Harrods ordered to pay woman £5,131 after losing Cartier bracelet refund case
Following the ruling, Harrods was ordered to pay Ms Romain £4,550 for the returned bracelet. With accumulated interest and court fees, the total amount awarded came to £5,131. The judge concluded that the case had turned on the evidence presented and that the defendants had failed to substantiate their position.
Judge Vignoli said: "This is a case which has turned very much on the evidence before the court and I am afraid to say that the defendants have been found wanting in this respect." She also stated that Harrods had "failed on the balance of probabilities" to prove that the bracelet had been returned with scratches.
Woman vowed never to shop at Harrods after £5,131 court win
Speaking outside court after the decision, Ms Romain described herself as "very relieved" by the outcome. She also made clear that the experience had changed her attitude towards shopping at the department store, saying: "I’m never buying from Harrods again."
She explained that she had spent years saving for the Cartier bracelet and had wanted to buy it as a birthday present for herself. "I was saving for years; I wanted to treat myself," she said. Reflecting on the outcome and the money she had spent, she added: "I’m going back to saving now. No more spending like this."
Disclaimer: This article is based on information reported by The Independent and publicly available court proceedings. The Times of India has not independently verified the claims, evidence or circumstances surrounding the dispute between Georgia Romain and Harrods. The account of the court's findings and the compensation awarded is based on the reported proceedings and should not be interpreted as an independent confirmation by Harrods or its representatives.

title: AI-generated python image triggers 48-hour emergency search in Italy
text:
A photograph showing a python emerging from a toilet prompted a 48-hour emergency search at an apartment in northern Italy, bringing firefighters and specialist officers to investigate a potentially dangerous reptile sighting. The image was shown by a nine-year-old boy who was visiting a friend's home in Castelfidardo, near Ancona. Responders searched the property but found no trace of the animal, raising the possibility that it had escaped. The mystery took an unexpected turn when officers examined the original photograph on the child's mobile phone. They discovered that the python had never been there and that the image had been created using artificial intelligence.
AI-generated toilet python photo prompts emergency search in Italy
The incident took place in Castelfidardo, a town near Ancona in Italy's Marche region. According to The Sun, the boy showed adults a photograph that appeared to capture a python inside the household toilet, claiming that the reptile had emerged from the bowl.
The apparent sighting prompted an immediate response. Firefighters arrived at the property and began checking the bathroom, where the snake was supposedly spotted. 
When their initial inspection produced no sign of the animal, the search was extended to other parts of the house.
There was also concern that the reptile might have moved away from the bathroom. Responders reportedly considered whether it could have escaped through an open window or found its way into a narrow opening elsewhere in the building. With no animal recovered, the possibility of an exotic snake remaining loose inside the property could not initially be ruled out.
Boy admits creating fake python sighting using artificial intelligence
The search continued into the following day, bringing in officers from Italy's military who specialise in dealing with exotic animals. Their involvement reflected the concern surrounding the possibility of a python being present inside a residential property. However, the investigation eventually shifted away from locating an animal and towards examining the photograph itself. Officers took a closer look at the original image stored on the child's mobile phone and discovered signs that it had been digitally generated.
The boy subsequently admitted that he had used an artificial intelligence application to add a python to a photograph of the toilet. There had been no actual snake in the bathroom. According to the account, he had been taking photographs while spending time with another child earlier that day. At some point, he used the AI application to alter one of the pictures, placing the reptile inside the toilet. He then presented the edited image to adults as though it documented a real encounter.
No criminal charges for nine-year-old as Italy's law sets age limit
The nine-year-old reportedly admitted what he had done after realising how seriously adults and emergency responders had taken the photograph. He also apologised for the alarm caused by the fabricated sighting.
Italian law does not allow children below the age of 14 to be held criminally responsible. As a result, the boy will not face criminal consequences over the incident, according to the report. The episode nevertheless attracted attention beyond the immediate search, particularly because the photograph had prompted a response involving several emergency and specialist teams.
Paolo Clini, director of the artificial intelligence department at Marche Polytechnic University, discussed the incident with local media. He described it as an example of how AI-generated material could trigger serious real-world consequences, particularly when people mistake fabricated images for genuine evidence. Clini also raised questions about a child's access to such technology. His concerns centred on how easily manipulated photographs could be circulated and how quickly they might be accepted as authentic, potentially prompting unnecessary emergency responses.
Disclaimer: This article is based on publicly available reports. The Times of India has not independently verified all details of the incident.

title: Canadian judge reopens luxury home dispute, cancels C$4.26 million damages order
text:
A Canadian judge has given a buyer another chance to defend himself in a dispute over an C$18 million property deal that fell through in 2021. The decision cancels a C$4.26 million order against Stephen Brown, who had agreed to buy the property from Rakesh Dhunna but did not complete the purchase.
Dhunna later sold the property for C$14.3 million, which was C$3.7 million less than the agreed price. He took Brown to court and secured an order for C$4,262,369.40 in compensation after the buyer failed to respond to the case.
Brown eventually approached the court to challenge the order. He argued that he had reasons to defend himself and also questioned how the seller's losses had been calculated.
In a decision dated March 25, Justice Stephens of the British Columbia Supreme Court allowed Brown to contest the claim. The judge cancelled the earlier orders and gave him 30 days to file his response.
Property sold for C$14.3 million
According to the informationa available in the 
judgment
, Brown and Dhunna signed the purchase agreement on April 17, 2021. The agreed price was C$18 million, but the sale did not go through.
Dhunna filed a case against Brown on September 16. Brown received the legal notice five days later but did not respond within the required 21 days.
As a result, Dhunna obtained a court order in November in his favour. 
The property was eventually sold in April 2023 for C$14.3 million.
Dhunna then sought compensation for the difference between the original sale price and the amount received from the later sale. He also included expenses incurred while holding the property. On July 18, 2023, the court ordered Brown to pay C$4,262,369.40.
Buyer disputes seller's losses
When Brown challenged the order, he questioned why Dhunna had not accepted an earlier offer for the property. He told the court that the seller had received an offer of C$14.8 million in February 2022 but did not accept it. The property was sold for C$14.3 million in April 2023.
Brown argued that accepting the earlier offer would have reduced the amount claimed against him by C$500,000. He also questioned the expenses of about C$562,369 that Dhunna had included for keeping the property until it was sold.
Buyer explains why he did not respond
Brown did not ask the court to cancel the earlier order until June 30, 2025, more than three years after it was issued. He had represented himself in the case until April 2025, when he hired a lawyer.
He told the court that he had not understood the legal process or realised that he could ask for the earlier decision to be reconsidered. He believed the property deal was no longer active and said he was also dealing with personal and financial difficulties.
Brown's affidavit mentioned the deaths of his father in Saskatchewan and his wife's niece in Oregon during this period.
The judge found that Brown had not deliberately ignored the original case. However, the court also noted that he had waited a long time before taking steps to challenge the order. His personal circumstances did not fully explain why he had allowed so much time to pass.
Dispute over purchase conditions
Brown also raised questions about the conditions attached to the original property agreement. Dhunna relied on an addendum dated April 23, 2021, which he said showed that Brown had agreed to remove certain conditions from the deal.
Brown acknowledged that the signature on the document appeared to be his but said he did not remember signing it. He denied agreeing to remove the conditions. The judge also noted that Dhunna's signature was missing from the document, although there was a space for it.
The court did not decide whether the conditions had been removed. However, the judge found that the disagreement needed to be examined further because it could affect whether Brown was required to complete the purchase.

title: Strong El Niño raises snow, avalanche & flood risks across Hindu Kush Himalaya
text:
An exceptionally strong El Niño is expected to persist through the winter and into early 2027, with forecasts pointing to normal to above-normal precipitation across much of the Hindu Kush Himalaya (HKH). The oceanic phenomenon could potentially bring more snow to parts of the western mountains while raising the risk of avalanches, landslides and localised flooding.
The HKH Winter Outlook 2026 report, jointly prepared by the Kathmandu-based International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD), Beijing Normal University and the Institute of Atmospheric Physics of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, says the El Niño is expected to strengthen further in the coming months. Its effects are likely to continue into February 2027.
Seasonal predictions indicate normal to above-normal precipitation across much of the HKH, including parts of Afghanistan, Pakistan, northern India, Nepal and China’s Xizang Autonomous Region. The outlook warns, however, that the impacts will vary across the region, with differences in precipitation, temperature, snowfall and fire danger.
El Niño and a wetter winter across the HKH
El Niño is a climate pattern linked to warmer-than-normal sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific. 
It can influence rainfall and temperature patterns across different parts of the world, including South Asia.
The outlook notes that the current El Niño has intensified sharply, with sea surface temperature anomalies in the central-eastern equatorial Pacific reaching 2.6°C above normal by mid-August 2026. Seasonal predictions indicate a very high likelihood of El Niño conditions continuing through February 2027.
The HKH’s winter weather is also shaped by western disturbances, which bring rain and snow to northwestern and northern India, Pakistan, Afghanistan and parts of Nepal. The outlook assesses the expected winter conditions using the HKH Sub-seasonal to Seasonal prediction system, alongside information from regional and global climate institutions.
Above-normal precipitation could improve soil moisture and support winter agriculture across parts of the region. In high-altitude catchments, precipitation is likely to fall as snow, contributing to the accumulation of snow that sustains river flows during the spring and summer.
But heavier precipitation could also increase the risk of avalanches, localised flooding and landslides, particularly in mountainous areas.
More snow in the west, less in parts of the east
The outlook projects above-normal snow depth across parts of the western HKH, particularly Afghanistan, Pakistan, northern India and Nepal. Below-normal snow depth is expected in parts of Bhutan and eastern Xizang.
Winter snow acts as a natural reservoir, supporting river flows and providing water for irrigation and hydropower in subsequent months. The report said the benefits would depend on how much snow accumulates, how long it persists and when it melts.
The forecast also indicates a mixed temperature pattern. Above-normal temperatures are likely across Afghanistan, Pakistan, northwestern India, Bangladesh and the hills of Nepal and southern Bhutan, while higher elevations in Nepal may experience cooler-than-normal conditions.
Despite the precipitation outlook, moderate to high forest and grassland fire hazards are expected in parts of the HKH, including Bhutan and Pakistan. High to very high fire danger is forecast in areas such as southeastern Xizang, Myanmar and parts of India.
Nepal and much of central and eastern India are expected to face low to very low fire danger.

title: Bangladesh garment sector lost $428 million in 18 days of unrest, finds survey
text:
DHAKA: Bangladesh's key export-earning ready-made garment sector suffered $428 million in production losses during 18 days of unrest, while buyers shifted orders worth another $254 million to competing countries, a preliminary industry survey found. The numbers, industry insiders said, were "worrying" for the world's second-largest apparel exporter. Bangladesh is behind only China and its closest competitors are Vietnam, Turkiye, India and Italy.
Meanwhile, PM Tarique Rahman proposed dialogue with "anti-fascist political parties" amid recent political violence, and massive protests and shutdowns by garment workers, demanding increase in wages, since Oct.
Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) Sunday said its survey covered the period from Nov 1-18 and collected responses from 317 garment factories that reported production disruptions due to the prevailing instability and various operational disruptions. "The affected factories incurred production losses amounting to $428 million in free-on-board (FOB) value during the period," it said.
 "The losses were compounded by difficulties in meeting shipment deadlines, leaving many export orders at risk. To retain orders and meet delivery commitments, factories were forced to resort to costly air shipments, offer substantial price discounts and, in some cases, face order cancellations," BGMEA said.
Without naming the competing countries, the survey said international buyers had shifted 59 million pieces of confirmed garment orders, worth $254 million, to other countries. BGMEA also expressed concern over the potential long-term damage to Bangladesh's reputation as a reliable sourcing destination in the global apparel market.

title: 17-year-old Canadian student directed film and used art for climate awareness
text:
At 17, Canadian student Melody Silva has found ways to bring environmental concerns beyond the classroom and into her wider community. From producing a documentary about fish farming and its effects on British Columbia’s wild salmon to speaking about climate injustice through live performances, she has used creative work to encourage people to pay attention to environmental issues. Her efforts also include working with Indigenous elders, supporting school recycling initiatives and helping other students find practical ways to take action against climate change.
Melody Silva used a documentary to highlight threats to wild salmon
Silva’s interest in environmental protection is closely connected to the natural surroundings in which she grew up. Living in an environment where nature was part of everyday life made it difficult for her to ignore the damage being done to it. She has described climate change as a particularly heavy concern for younger generations, who are left to deal with problems created before their time.
According to the National Youth Climate Activism Awards Association, Silva restarted her high school Earth Club 3 years ago. The initiative gave her an opportunity to turn environmental concerns into activities that other students could participate in.
One of her most significant projects came in the spring of 2024, when she directed and produced a documentary examining the harmful effects of fish farming on British Columbia’s wild salmon population. 
The film also explored the wider consequences for the coastal ecosystem, recognising that the health of salmon populations is connected to the natural environment around them.
Rather than relying on research alone, Silva sought perspectives from people with direct knowledge of the issue. She interviewed two Kwak’waka’wakw elders and Dan Lewis, executive director of the environmental non-profit Clayoquot Action.
The documentary was produced with help from Clayoquot Action and filmmaker Jérémy Mathieu. Silva subsequently presented it at her school to introduce fellow students to the concerns surrounding fish farming and wild salmon.
GISS Earth Club members Kaelyn Dennis and Melody Silva sort through bags of school trash to determine what could be recycled.  Image Credit: Robb Magley/Gulf Island Driftwood
How did she bring climate concerns to a wider audience through art
She has also used performing arts to reach people who might not otherwise engage with climate issues.
Her profile on the National Youth Climate Activism Awards Association website explains that she competed in the national finals of the Canadian Improv Games. During the competition, she used the stage to speak about climate injustice, bringing environmental concerns into a creative setting.
The performance reached an audience beyond those attending in person. It was staged at the National Arts Centre and livestreamed, allowing viewers across Canada to watch. This gave Silva another opportunity to communicate her concerns and show how art could become a useful platform for discussing environmental problems.
School activities became another part of her environmental work
Silva’s involvement in climate action has also extended into everyday school life. Her work with the Earth Club has included organising activities that encourage students to reconsider how they consume, reuse and dispose of everyday items.
According to her 2026 youth climate activism profile, she has spent 4 years volunteering with Transition Salt Spring, a local environmental non-profit. The experience influenced how she approached her responsibilities as an Earth Club leader.
She introduced several eco-events, including clothing swaps, gift swaps and repair cafés. These activities offer students alternatives to throwing away items that remain useful. Clothing and gifts can find new owners, while damaged belongings can be repaired instead of being immediately discarded.
She also encouraged other students to take part in climate action
Her youth climate activism profile describes a Youth Climate Advocacy Training Programme that she was spearheading at her school. One of its planned outcomes was the development and implementation of a plastic recycling system at Gulf Islands Secondary School. Silva intended to collect information about how much waste the programme could divert from landfill.
Her longer-term aim was to persuade the school administration to introduce permanent plastic recycling facilities. She also hoped the initiative could provide an example for other schools across British Columbia.
Her inspiration comes from both her upbringing and her family history. Silva mentioned that her grandfather was among the main organisers of the Mears Island logging protests. Seeing the outcome of those efforts gave her confidence that collective environmental action could make a difference.
Her plans extend beyond school climate campaigns
According to the 2026 profile, she planned to attend the University of Victoria to study Geography with a minor in Environmental Studies. She hopes to pursue a law degree afterwards and become an environmental lawyer.
She has also gained experience through scientific research. She led a preliminary research team studying the relationship between moss and soil microorganisms for the Salt Spring Climate Adaptation Research Lab. The work helped scientists studying Mount Maxwell identify an overall lack of microorganism activity in the soil, which they planned to investigate further.

title: Meet the Mississippi mechanic who transformed himself into the Rhinestone Cowboy
text:
In rural Mississippi, a mechanic who had spent much of his life getting by on modest means began an unusual personal transformation in 1975. Inspired by 
Glen Campbell
's hit song Rhinestone Cowboy, Loy Bowlin adopted a new identity and began decorating his clothes with sequins. The transformation took years, turning an ordinary house into an elaborate display that extended from its rooms to parts of its exterior. Bowlin, who became known as the Rhinestone Cowboy, died in 1995. His work did not disappear with him, however. Several parts of the house, along with his distinctive clothing and furniture, were eventually transferred to a museum in Wisconsin, as reported by Kohler Foundation.
Loy Bowlin's early life in rural Mississippi before the Rhinestone Cowboy
Born in 1909 in Franklin County, Mississippi, Bowlin grew up in a rural setting where money was often scarce. He married Ina Mae Mitchell in 1933, and the couple farmed, while Bowlin also earned money by selling scrap metal. Their marriage ended in the 1950s. Following the separation, Bowlin experienced a difficult period, with depression becoming part of his life.
His Christian faith offered him some comfort during those years. 
By the middle of the 1970s, he was looking for a way to change his circumstances and how he felt about himself.
How Glen Campbell inspired the Rhinestone Cowboy
In 1975, Bowlin began developing a new identity after being inspired by Glen Campbell's song Rhinestone Cowboy. The record, released in 1975, gave him the name around which he built his new appearance.
Reportedly, he began decorating his outfits, turning ordinary suits and hats into brightly embellished pieces. Rhinestones, glitter and reflective materials became regular features of his clothing. His appearance gradually became part of a much larger undertaking, one that would eventually take over his home.
Bowlin was no longer simply adding decorative details to a few personal belongings. He was creating an environment in which the same visual style appeared across his clothes, furniture and surroundings.
A house transformed with glitter, photographs and found objects
The house became the centre of Bowlin's artistic work. Over approximately five years, he covered its interior and sections of the outside with an assortment of decorative materials. There was little distinction between conventional craft supplies and everyday objects. Cut-out paper, painted designs, rhinestones, aluminium foil, tinsel, Christmas decorations and collaged images from magazines all became part of the composition.
The surfaces were built up with bright colours and intricate arrangements. Photographs and magazine illustrations appeared alongside glittering decorations, while strands of tinsel and ornaments added another layer to the rooms. Rather than following a conventional approach to decorating a house, Bowlin treated its walls and furnishings as places where his ideas could take shape.
The result was closely connected to the persona he had adopted after hearing Campbell's song. His clothes and home belonged to the same creative world, with the rhinestone-covered suits and decorated rooms reflecting one another.
What happened to the house after Bowlin's death
Bowlin died in 1995, but his decorated home remained on the property. Preserving it in its original location, however, was not possible. Houston-based artist and collector Katy Emde acquired the house after his death, with an important condition attached to the purchase: the structure had to be removed from the site.
Emde documented the property before taking it apart. The process allowed the different components of Bowlin's creation to be recorded and retained rather than simply discarded. In 1998, Kohler Foundation, Inc. acquired the collection of dismantled materials.
The foundation later gifted the preserved components to the John Michael Kohler Arts Center in Sheboygan, Wisconsin. The transfer included parts of the house as well as many of Bowlin's customised suits, hats and furniture.
Preserving the work at a Wisconsin arts centre
The John Michael Kohler Arts Center became the home of material from Bowlin's unusual project. Its collection preserved elements of an environment that had originally been assembled in a private Mississippi residence, allowing the work to be retained beyond the lifespan of the building itself.
The preservation also brought together different aspects of Bowlin's creative output. His clothing, furniture and architectural decorations were all part of the same undertaking, rather than separate collections of objects. Keeping these pieces together helped retain the connection between the man, the identity he created and the home he spent years transforming.

title: 12-year-old twins turn playroom into custom toy business with 3D printer
text:
Aaron Osirus is 12 years old and already runs a business from his playroom. He noticed that many classmates carried fidget toys at school and decided to make his own. He borrowed $600 from his parents to buy a 3D printer with an automatic material system that can switch colours during printing, then began selling custom toys to classmates and neighbourhood kids. His twin brother, Alain, later joined him in running A3D. The twins earn about $200 in profit each month after paying for supplies and labour. Advanced Manufacturing gives the same monthly figure.
How Aaron Osirus turned a $600 loan into a custom 3D-printed toy factory
According to CBS News, the idea came after Aaron noticed that many of his classmates carried fidget toys at school. He told the outlet he wondered why he could not make them himself, since they were all plastic: "If all these fidgets are plastic, why can't I make them?" Aaron noticed that a lot of his classmates were always playing with fidget spinners. That gave him the idea to make his own and sell them to other students, and A3D was born.
Aaron borrowed $600 from his parents to buy a high-tech 3D printer. The machine has an automatic material system that can switch colours during the printing process.
According to Advanced Manufacturing, the $600 loan from his parents paid for the 3D printer and the filament to make spinners and small toys. CBS News Atlanta reports that Aaron began by selling toys to classmates and neighbourhood kids. 
He customised each order to the customer's preferred design, size and colour, and then set a price and a delivery timeline.
How twin brothers Aaron and Alain Osirus run their custom toy factory
As demand grew, Aaron brought his twin brother, Alain Osirus, into the business. Alain says he is a designer for A3D, that he sometimes makes the toys and that he helps with marketing. He also checks how long each item takes, the cost and the fulfilment.
The brothers produce popular items such as pass-through fidgets and articulated toys. Their most expensive product is a four-colour kitten that takes about a full day to print and sells for $5. Advanced Manufacturing says the brothers describe the kitten as their most popular item after fidget spinners and that it takes all day to print. Both outlets report that regular customers receive a 50-cent discount.
$600 investment turned into a profitable toy business for two young brothers
The twins earn about $200 in profit each month after paying for supplies and labour. The outlet adds that, according to industry leaders PrintPal and SelfCAD, profit margins on 3D-printed products can range from 70% to 90% because the raw materials are relatively inexpensive. The brothers also keep costs down by asking friends whether they would like to volunteer before hiring additional help. The brothers figure they make about $200 in profit every month and rely on volunteers instead of employees.
Aaron finds it rewarding to watch people play with his prints: "Oh yeah, that's really cool because I made it." CBS News Atlanta reports that the twins say the business has strengthened their bond and taught them lessons about investing, customer service and entrepreneurship. Aaron encourages other young people to follow their dreams and try their hardest, and says they need to save up the money and plan for everything. Alain also urges others to chase their dreams.

title: NY landlord banned after 16 children suffer lead poisoning in his properties
text:
A landlord’s failure to address a hidden danger inside homes has now cost him his place in New York’s rental housing market. At least 16 children suffered lead poisoning while living in properties owned by Syracuse landlord William D’Angelo, whose repeated failure to eliminate hazardous lead paint conditions has prompted state authorities to take decisive action. Following violations of an earlier court settlement, D’Angelo must sell his remaining rental properties and will be permanently barred from owning or managing residential rentals across New York.
Court action follows repeated violations
According to the New York State Attorney General’s Office, Attorney General Letitia James announced the agreement after D’Angelo failed to comply with a February 2024 court-approved settlement worth $310,000. The agreement had required him to address lead hazards at 18 designated priority properties by December 2025.
The latest settlement resolves a contempt proceeding initiated by the Attorney General’s Office in August 2026 after repeated warnings failed to secure compliance.
The original legal action dates back to 2023, when the Attorney General’s Office, Onondaga County and the City of Syracuse sued D’Angelo. An investigation identified approximately 336 lead-based paint violations across nearly two dozen properties, with at least 16 children recording elevated blood lead levels.
More concerns were raised about unsafe repairs
D'Angelo paid restitution to affected families under the 2024 settlement. Later, his efforts to remove remaining threats stalled.
A June 2026 inspection by Syracuse city officials identified continuing violations. Investigators also discovered that D’Angelo had undertaken lead-related repair work himself without employing an Environmental Protection Agency (EPA)-certified contractor, following an approved work plan or securing the required independent monitoring.
The court subsequently determined that he had violated the original judgment. Although some violations have since been corrected, lead hazards remain at 10 of the 18 priority properties, according to the Attorney General’s Office.
New agreement puts properties under scrutiny
Under the latest agreement, D’Angelo must sell all his remaining rental properties within 180 days. Every prospective buyer will require approval from the Attorney General’s Office in coordination with Syracuse and Onondaga County authorities.
Buyers acquiring properties with unresolved lead hazards must commit to completing remediation through EPA-certified professionals. Repairs must be finished within 60 days of purchase for occupied homes and 120 days for vacant properties.
New owners cannot collect rent from existing tenants or rent out vacant units until all identified lead hazards have been eliminated. If an occupied property remains unsold after 90 days, D’Angelo must arrange and finance the necessary repairs himself using certified contractors and an approved monitor.
Financial penalties and a wider public health concern
The agreement imposes a penalty of $100 per day for each property where deadlines or other requirements are breached. D’Angelo could also face a $37,500 penalty for every property where he performs lead remediation himself instead of hiring certified professionals. State Supreme Court Justice Joseph Lamendola has warned that further violations could result in additional consequences, including imprisonment.
Finger Lakes Daily News reported that D’Angelo owned or managed at least 48 Syracuse rental properties containing 116 units over three decades. All were constructed before 1940, making them presumed to contain lead-based paint.
The Attorney General’s Office has also highlighted the wider scale of the problem. During the first half of 2026, 9.4 per cent of Syracuse children tested had elevated blood lead levels. 
In 2025, testing identified elevated levels in 158 Black children, compared with 56 white children.
The latest agreement marks another step in New York's efforts to address childhood lead exposure. Once D’Angelo completes the sale of his remaining properties, his removal from the state's residential rental market will be permanent.
