title: Cameraman Wins $44,000: Salameh gives mother GTA 6 winnings; survives 60-minute robbery mission
text:
A video game robbery rarely leads to a life-changing moment outside the screen. However, MrBeast found a way to make it happen. The YouTube star offered real cash for every dollar his longtime cameraman, Tareq Salameh, could steal in GTA 6. What began as a race against police, security guards and a ticking clock soon became a personal mission. Salameh wanted to use the opportunity to give something back to his mother. After an intense 60-minute challenge, he walked away with approximately $44,000 for her, turning a gaming stunt into an emotional family moment.
Tareq Salameh fights setbacks in MrBeast’s GTA 6 challenge
The challenge featured in MrBeast Gaming's November 20 video, titled 'Whatever You Steal in GTA 6, You Keep!' The timing also added to the excitement, as the video arrived just one day after Rockstar Games released GTA 6.
Salameh entered the challenge with one clear goal. He wanted to earn as much as possible for his mother, who had supported him throughout his life.
'I'm, like, literally not joking. I'm doing this for my mom. I don't care how high it is,' he said.
Salameh, who was born in Saudi Arabia to Palestinian-Jordanian parents, moved to the United States as a child. He credited his mother with helping him adjust to his new surroundings, including teaching him English.
'She taught me everything. She taught me how to speak English. You know what I mean? I love my mom,' he said.
However, the challenge came with strict conditions. Every dollar stolen in GTA 6 counted towards the real-life payout, but getting arrested or killed would erase his entire balance. He also could not deposit his money in a bank to protect it.
His final task was equally difficult. He had to get aboard an aircraft and take off before the 60-minute timer expired.
MrBeast’s $44,000 GTA 6 challenge ends with an emotional payoff
Salameh initially built a strong balance by robbing a jewellery store, collecting more than $5,000. However, an attempted robbery at a loan store in Little Cuba nearly ended his chances. Armed security guards killed his character, wiping out everything he had earned.
Instead of giving up, he returned to the challenge and started building his total again. He stole vehicles, sold them for cash, broke into a Fleeca bank vault and targeted more businesses.
Eventually, his earnings crossed $44,000. But the biggest obstacle was still ahead.
With police chasing him and time running out, Salameh hijacked a bus at the airport and rushed towards a passenger aircraft. MrBeast urged him to forget about earning more money and focus on escaping before the deadline.
Salameh managed to get airborne just in time, securing the promised payout. His mother's reaction made the achievement even more meaningful, as she called him 'the best son ever'.
While the video also featured a promotion for financial technology platform Step, the challenge's emotional centre remained Salameh's decision to use his gaming skills to reward the person who had done so much for him.
For him, the biggest win was never the money inside GTA 6. It was the chance to give his mother a real $44,000 surprise.

title: Watch: Russian warship bursts into flames in suspected Ukraine drone attack in Libya
text:
A suspected Ukrainian sea drone attack struck a Russian navy warship at the port of Benghazi in eastern Libya, triggering an explosion and fire and leaving the vessel partially submerged.
The ship, identified as the Russian corvette Merkury, was docked at the port to refuel and take on supplies under a cooperation agreement between Moscow and the eastern-based Libyan administration. Satellite imagery shared by imagery provider Vantor showed that most of the vessel had capsized and sunk, with only its bow visible above water. Smoke and debris were also seen around the ship.
Two Libyan military officials told the Associated Press that Ukrainian sea drones had been launched at the warship from a base operated by Ukrainian forces in western Libya. At least four drones were intercepted, while two struck the vessel, they said. Neither Ukraine nor Russia has commented on the attack.
Meanwhile, local sources told Al Jazeera that an unknown number of Libyan and Russian nationals were killed. They also claimed the vessel was carrying weapons, ammunition and drones. Residents reportedly saw three drones attack the ship. These claims have not been publicly confirmed.
The eastern-based Libyan administration said the fire had been brought under control and launched a joint investigation with Russia to establish the source of the attack. It condemned the suspected strike as a violation of Libya's sovereignty and a threat to maritime safety.
"The Libyan government will not allow Libyan ports, territory or territorial waters to be turned into an arena for settling scores or exporting international conflicts," it said, adding that Libya was "not a party to the Russian-Ukrainian war".
Earlier, in a separate incident on Sunday evening, a sea drone struck a Malta-flagged commercial vessel off Benghazi. The eastern administration's Health Ministry said all crew members injured in the attack had been rescued and were receiving treatment. Almasar television reported that naval and air forces destroyed at least 12 other sea drones off the Mediterranean city.
The western-based Libyan government also expressed concern over attempts to involve the country's ports and civilian facilities in external conflicts.
Ukraine's 'presence' in Libya
The suspected attack comes amid reports of Ukrainian military and intelligence personnel operating in western Libya. Middle East security and defence expert Tallha Abdulrazaq told Al Jazeera that Ukrainian intelligence services were most likely behind the strike.
"There was a lot of reporting on the tail end of last year about there being a deal between the Ukrainian intelligence services and the Tripolitan government to establish a Ukrainian military and intelligence presence there," he said.
"In exchange, the Tripoli government would get Ukrainian military expertise," he added.
Libya has remained divided between rival administrations since a NATO-backed uprising toppled longtime leader Muammar Gaddafi in 2011. A UN-recognised government is based in Tripoli, while a rival administration controls the east.
The head of the eastern-based Libyan government, Osama Hammad, has sought an international investigation, asking the UN to examine whether the drones were launched from western Libya and verify reports of Ukrainian experts operating in the country.

title: Wife's support during husband's medical training becomes key in divorce asset battle
text:
An Alabama appeals court has overturned part of a divorce settlement after finding that a lower court wrongly excluded a surgeon's medical-business investments from the couple's marital assets. The woman had worked and helped meet household expenses while her husband completed medical training. The case has now been sent back for a fresh assessment of the couple's property.
Sarah Gordon and Charles Gordon married in 2011, the year Charles completed medical school. He subsequently underwent an internship, a five-year orthopaedic surgery residency and a spine-surgery fellowship. During this period, Sarah worked as a nanny and took up other jobs to help pay household expenses.
Charles completed his fellowship in 2018, after which the couple moved to Baldwin County. He joined Baldwin Bone and Joint, an orthopaedic practice, and became a partner in 2020 or 2021 after borrowing money from First Horizon Bank. Sarah, meanwhile, became a full-time homemaker and had no separate income.
In its November 20, decision, the Alabama Court of Civil Appeals 
ruled
 that the husband's business interests should have been considered marital property. 
It reversed the property division and directed the lower court to determine their value and reconsider the distribution. However, it did not specify what share Sarah should receive.
Financial disputes during divorce
Sarah filed for divorce in February 2024. The trial court subsequently ordered the couple to maintain their existing financial arrangements and prohibited them from disposing of assets acquired during the marriage without permission.
Sarah later accused Charles of restricting her access to bank accounts and credit cards. She also alleged that he had withdrawn around $183,000 from their joint checking account.
Under a temporary agreement adopted by the court in October 2024, Charles was required to place the withdrawn money in an interest-bearing account, resume depositing his salary into the joint account and transfer another $20,000. He was also directed to restore Sarah's access to their financial accounts.
Sarah subsequently alleged that Charles had issued three cheques totalling $19,400 after depositing the additional money. She also complained that he had again restricted her access to the joint account.
Charles admitted during the trial that he had stopped depositing his salary into the account around May 2024 and again around February 2025. He also acknowledged removing Sarah as an authorised credit-card user, saying her spending exceeded what he could afford.
Court rejects request to postpone trial
In October 2025, Sarah sought $30,000 towards expert assistance and legal expenses, saying she needed professionals to examine her husband's assets.
The final hearing was scheduled for December 8, 2025. Three days before the trial, she sought a postponement, saying she could not afford a forensic accountant and had recently discovered a bank account and credit card for which she had not received records.
The trial judge rejected the request, noting that the divorce case had been pending since February 2024.
The appeals court upheld that decision. It said Sarah had raised the need for expert assistance in October but waited until shortly before the hearing to seek a postponement. Her lawyer had also failed to explain what an accountant might discover or how the findings would affect the case.
Medical businesses should be included 
The main issue in the appeal was Charles's ownership interests in Baldwin Bone and Joint, a surgery centre and other medical consulting businesses.
During the trial, Sarah submitted an assessment estimating that Charles's 15.38% interest in Baldwin Bone and Joint Medical Center, LLC, was worth $219,491. The calculation was based on a September 2025 balance sheet.
The lower court admitted the document but treated the business as Charles's separate estate. It also declined to accept a tax document relating to the surgery centre as a valuation. Charles had invested $150,000 in that centre but maintained that its shares were "worth nothing" because the business was operating at a loss.
The appeals court found that the business interests had been acquired during the marriage. Charles completed his medical training seven years after the wedding and purchased his medical-practice partnership interest in 2020 or 2021. There was no evidence that he had acquired these interests before marriage or received them through gifts or inheritance.
Under the law, property accumulated during marriage can form part of the marital estate. The appeals court said the lower court had no sufficient evidence to classify the businesses as Charles's separate property.
Charles argued that the lower court had already accounted for the investments through a $70,000 property settlement awarded to Sarah. However, that payment covered several matters, including retirement-account adjustments, moving expenses and his violations of earlier court orders.
The lower court had neither valued the businesses nor specified how much of the settlement was intended to compensate Sarah for them. The appeals court therefore found that the payment did not correct the error in excluding the businesses from the marital estate.
Home, vehicle and alimony issues
The appeals court also addressed the couple's marital home. The lower court had recorded its equity as $100,000, describing the figure as an agreement between the parties. Sarah disputed this and argued that the equity was $150,000, based on a $1.5 million appraisal and a $1.35 million mortgage.
The appeals court found no clear agreement on the amount and directed the lower court to determine the equity from the evidence.
It also ordered the lower court to consider the Mercedes G-Wagon, which had been excluded because it belonged to an LLC, alongside the valuation of the business interests.
The court left the decision not to award Sarah a vehicle unchanged because she had testified that she did not hold a valid driving licence at the time of the trial.
It also allowed the lower court to reconsider alimony after completing the revised property division, as the two issues are connected.
The appeals court upheld the refusal to postpone the trial and the decision not to hold Charles in contempt or impose additional sanctions.
It ultimately reversed the division of marital property and sent the case back to the Baldwin Circuit Court. The lower court must now value the medical-business interests, include them in the marital estate and reconsider an equitable division of the couple's assets.

title: Could IShowSpeed have a future beyond YouTube? Usain Bolt weighs in after surprising 100m performance
text:
IShowSpeed has made a name for himself as one of the most popular YouTube streamers, but could he also have a future in professional sports? The internet star recently got the chance to show his running skills in front of eight-time Olympic champion 
Usain Bolt
. During their latest meeting, Speed ran the 100-meter race in an impressive 10.352 seconds. His performance caught attention, and Bolt was seen reacting positively to the result. The moment has now started conversations about Speed's future in sprinting.
IShowSpeed clocks an impressive 10.35 seconds in 100m race in front of Usain Bolt
The 100-meter race took place in IShowSpeed's November 22, 2026, YouTube video titled 
"I RACED USAIN BOLT!" The video is part of the second season of his series called Speed Goes Pro. In this series, Speed gets help from famous athletes as he tries to learn their sports and improve his skills.
IShowSpeed ran the 100 meters in 10.352 seconds in the video. That is a solid time for someone without track experience. It takes a lot of strength and training to achieve that.
He got to train with Usain Bolt this time. Bolt is the fastest man in the world and holds the 100-meter world record at 9.58 seconds. He also has 8 Olympic gold medals.
The timing got people talking right away. Some viewers began wondering if the YouTube star could do more than entertain people online.
Could Usain Bolt's advice help IShowSpeed become a professional sprinter?
One of the biggest highlights of the video was Usain Bolt's reaction to Speed's performance. The Olympic legend seemed impressed by his run and acknowledged that the streamer could have the potential to become a professional sprinter.
A speed comparison graph shared after the race also revealed an interesting detail. IShowSpeed recorded a higher speed in miles per hour than Bolt during the first 15 meters of the sprint. This suggests that Speed showed strong acceleration at the start of the race.
However, this does not mean Speed was faster than Bolt over the entire 100 meters. Bolt still holds the world record of 9.58 seconds and has years of professional sprinting experience.
For Speed, getting praise from someone like Bolt is still a big moment. It also gives him a chance to learn from one of the greatest runners in history.
In the end, IShowSpeed's 10.352-second run has given fans another reason to talk about his athletic skills. Whether he chooses to follow professional sprinting in the future remains to be seen, but his latest performance has certainly caught the attention of the sporting world.

title: Kick streamer CostaKid sparks controversy after attacking woman in viral livestream clip
text:
Kick streamer CostaKid has become the subject of online criticism after a video showed him getting into a physical fight with a woman during a livestream. The incident reportedly took place inside a car after the woman poured water over his head. CostaKid, 20, quickly turned around and reacted angrily. The video shows him throwing an object at her, spitting on her, grabbing her hair and hitting her several times. The incident has sparked a debate about his violent reaction.
CostaKid attacks woman after she pours water over his head during livestream
The incident happened while CostaKid was livestreaming from inside a car. According to reports, the woman poured water over his head as a prank. However, the streamer did not take it well and quickly lost his temper.
After the water was poured on him, CostaKid turned around and started fighting with the woman. He reportedly threw something at her before spitting on her and grabbing her by the hair. The video then showed him hitting her several times.
People who were present during the incident could be heard shouting at CostaKid and asking him to stop. However, the fight quickly became the main topic of discussion after the clip started spreading on social media.
The video has drawn strong reactions from viewers. While some people have pointed out that pouring water on someone without their permission was wrong, others believe that CostaKid's physical reaction was far too extreme.
Kick streamer CostaKid faces backlash after viral fight with woman
Following the incident, CostaKid has faced criticism from people discussing the video online. Many viewers have questioned his actions and believe that the woman pouring water on him did not justify the way he reacted.
The incident has also brought attention to the streamer's previous legal trouble. According to a report, CostaKid was arrested in Miami the previous month and charged with aggravated assault with a deadly weapon.
CostaKid is a 20-year-old streamer from Suffolk, England. He has gained more than 500,000 followers across platforms such as TikTok, Kick and Instagram.
The latest livestream incident has added to the attention surrounding his online activities. Some viewers have also questioned whether he could face further legal trouble following the fight. However, there is no confirmed information about any new arrest or charges related to this incident.
For now, the viral clip continues to attract attention, with viewers debating the actions of both people involved. While the water prank may have upset CostaKid, his reported physical response has become the biggest talking point.

title: Why did a small GTA 6 streamer break down in tears after Ibai Llanos joined his Twitch stream?
text:
A small streamer named Dicrim_RD69 had an emotional moment after Twitch star Ibai Llanos joined his GTA 6 livestream and helped him reach thousands of viewers. The Dominican streamer had been playing the game with almost no one watching when Ibai discovered his broadcast on November 19. After joining the stream, Ibai asked his followers to visit the channel, follow Dicrim and keep him company. The shoutout quickly changed the stream, bringing in more than 3,200 viewers within hours.
How did Ibai Llanos help a GTA 6 streamer go from zero to over 3,200 viewers?
Dicrim_RD69 was streaming GTA 6 when Ibai Llanos came across his broadcast. At that time, the small streamer had no viewers watching him. Ibai joined the livestream and simply wrote,
"Hello."
However, Ibai did much more than just visit the channel. He shared Dicrim's stream with his followers on social media and asked them to visit, follow and spend some time with the small creator.
The response was much bigger than Dicrim could have expected. His viewer count quickly increased and reached 3,243 people within a few hours. For a streamer who was used to playing in front of almost nobody, seeing thousands of people watching him was an unforgettable moment.
Dicrim became emotional when he saw the sudden support. He thanked Ibai and said that he had been a fan of the Spanish streamer for a long time. He also told the viewers, 
"You guys have brought me to tears."
Why did the small GTA 6 streamer get emotional during his call with Ibai?
During a video call with Ibai, Dicrim explained that he had been streaming for more than a year but had struggled to attract viewers. He said that playing and streaming without anyone to talk to sometimes made him feel sad. He was especially upset the night before Ibai found his channel.
Dicrim also shared that his family could not afford video games when he was younger. This made the moment even more special for him, as he finally had thousands of people watching him play a game he enjoyed.
Ibai understood how Dicrim felt because he had also started small. He remembered that when he was 14, he used to stream basketball commentary with his cousin. Just like Dicrim, they also had no viewers at the beginning.
Ibai encouraged the young streamer to continue doing what made him happy. He told Dicrim,
"If it makes you happy, keep doing it."
The advice came from someone who had experienced the same struggle before becoming a major name in online streaming.
In the end, Dicrim's story became a reminder that even a small act of support can make a big difference to a new creator. Ibai's visit gave him a huge audience, but it also made him feel that his hard work had finally been noticed. For Dicrim, the day was about much more than reaching 3,243 viewers; it was about feeling supported after a long time of streaming alone.

title: Alaska Supreme Court upholds $3,780 child support after dentist understated income
text:
A financial disclosure that initially resulted in a father’s monthly child support payment being less than $700 became the focus of a legal fight over income transparency and parental responsibility. A dentist in Alaska claimed his earnings were $36,960, but it turned out he was making substantially more, which led to a dramatic hike in child support payments for his four children. The Alaska Supreme Court has now upheld the new order, ruling that parents cannot take advantage of protections against retroactive child support changes to benefit from knowingly underreporting their income.
Legal dispute over income difference
According to the Alaska Supreme Court’s decision in Bowen v. Ray, 2 No. S-18430 (Nov. 20, 2026), Doug Bowen is a pediatric dentist and member of the Alaska Army National Guard who separated from his wife, Deana Ray, in March 2022. Two months later, Ray filed for divorce.
During the course of the proceedings, both parties submitted financial information to determine child support. Bowen reported earning $36,960 a year. In January 2023, the Palmer Superior Court ordered Bowen to pay $697.94 a month for their four children, who are mostly in Ray’s care.
But Ray later disputed the calculation, saying Bowen had not included several sources of income in his financial disclosures.
Documents reveal substantially larger earnings
In describing the proceedings, the Alaska Supreme Court said Ray submitted tax documents showing Bowen earned about $183,688 from his private dental practice in 2021. She also submitted employment records indicating he started with Southcentral Foundation in September 2022 with an annual salary of about $176,000.
The higher-paying employment was supported by Bowen’s own testimony at the divorce trial. His pay records showed gross monthly earnings of about $13,266, plus a $17,247 sign-on bonus.
The lower court also considered business deductions claimed by Bowen, among them accelerated depreciation. It found the deductions were not enough to justify discounting his much higher income in setting child support.
Increase in monthly payments for back pay
In September 2023, the Superior Court found that Bowen's income exceeded the applicable Alaska child support guideline amount of $126,000. This increased his monthly obligation from $697.94 to $3,780 effective October 1, 2022, when he had started his higher paying job.
Bowen appealed, claiming the increase violated Alaska Civil Rule 90.3, which generally bars retroactive changes in child support obligations.
The Alaska Supreme Court rejected that argument, noting that the restriction was not intended to protect people who knowingly misrepresent their financial circumstances.
Supreme Court dismisses retroactivity argument
In a Nov. 20, 2026, decision, the Alaska Supreme Court ruled that the state’s restrictions on retroactively changing child support do not extend to instances of intentional financial misrepresentation.
The judges said the original order was based on misleading income information and allowing the lower payment to stand would undermine the purpose of child support protections. The court noted the rules were designed to ensure children receive appropriate financial support and not to shield parents who knowingly provide false financial disclosures.
The Supreme Court therefore affirmed the lower court’s decision to apply the higher payments as of October 2022, when Bowen began his higher-paying job.
Property dispute adds another dimension
The appeal also concerned Silver Springs, a commercial property legally owned by Bowen’s parents, which they purchased for his dental practice.
The lower court determined that during the marriage, Bowen had been paying his parents about $2,000 each month, with the understanding that eventually he would own the property.
Bowen argued the payments were for rent and other unpaid debts, but the Alaska Supreme Court ruled there was enough evidence to support the lower court decision that payments had created an equity interest in the marital estate.
The judges therefore agreed with the ruling that that equity was to be treated as marital property subject to division in the divorce.
Earlier support adjustment separate
The Alaska Supreme Court also noted a later order, issued in February 2024, lowered Bowen’s monthly child support obligation to $1,562.81 after a change in the custody arrangement between the parents. But that adjustment wasn’t included in the appeal.
The state's highest court, in its final ruling on the matter, upheld the lower court's conclusions on the divisions of marital property and the child support computations, leaving unchanged the decisions that were contested.

title: Welsh glamping-site owner faces £135,000 legal bill over disputed driveway
text:
A Welsh glamping site owner has been ordered to pay £135,000 in legal costs after a dispute over whether her neighbours can drive past their front door to reach their own parking space. Carol Esteban is now challenging the ruling at the Court of Appeal, according to AOL and The Independent.
The case centres on a shared track at Cwmtawe Farm near Abercrave, close to the Brecon Beacons. Esteban argued that the neighbours’ right of way ended opposite their front door, while Neil and Nadine Gould said it extended far enough for them to park beside their home.
How the dispute began
The Goulds’ detached cottage, Cwmtawe Villa, is surrounded by land belonging to Cwmtawe Farm, where Esteban runs a glamping site across more than 60 acres. The properties were once held by the same owner, but the villa was sold off in 1949 and the original documents have been lost.
A 1964 conveyancing document gave the villa’s owners an easement, allowing them to use the farm track on foot or by vehicle. The problem was that the map attached to that document was missing the letter B, which was meant to mark where the right of way ended. Esteban argued that the right of way stopped at the front door of the villa. 
The Goulds argued that it extended a few feet further, allowing them to turn into the hardstanding parking area beside their house.
What the court decided
In July 2025, Judge Milwyn Jarman ruled in favour of the Goulds. He found that their vehicular right of way extended to the space on the north side of the villa, where they currently park.
The judge rejected Esteban’s argument that the right of way should stop at the front door. He said that interpretation would lead to impracticality, since the Goulds would be able to drive up to the door but not park or turn around. The court also ordered Esteban to pay £135,000 in legal costs. That figure has now become part of the appeal.
Why the appeal matters
Esteban’s lawyers argue that the High Court judge did not properly interpret the 1949 conveyance. They say the judge instead decided what the parties should have agreed to, rather than what the documents actually said, as per the reports. They also argue that there is no evidence the track extended beyond the front door of Cwmtawe. The appeal focuses on whether the easement stops at the front door or allows the Goulds to reach their parking spaces.
Esteban’s legal team also challenges the costs order. They point out that she succeeded on parts of her counterclaim, including a finding that a waterpipe had been installed unlawfully on her land.
What the neighbours say
The Goulds’ lawyers argue that the judge reached the right conclusion. They say the easement must allow the couple to reach their parking spaces, otherwise it would have little practical use.
They argue that the layout of the land shows there is no physical feature stopping the Goulds from driving onto their parking area. The lawyers say the judge’s interpretation gives practical effect to what the original grantor intended.
The appeal judges have reserved their decision. The outcome will determine whether the Goulds can continue using the track to access their parking space, and whether Esteban will have to pay the £135,000 costs bill.
